author: Staff and agencies
description:
Assessment of damage is underway, days after two attacks that destroyed road section of key bridge across Kerch strait linking annexed peninsula to Russia

The bridge connecting annexed Crimea to Russia has been attacked again, a local Russian official said on Wednesday, two days after Ukrainian strikes caused serious damage to the infrastructure.

The ‌attack is third this week on the bridge which ‌connects mainland Russia with Crimea which ​it annexed from Ukraine in 2014. The strike is a ⁠major blow to ​President ​Vladimir Putin ​ahead of ​his meetings ‌with US ​and ​China counterparts on Thursday.

Continue reading...
title: Crimea bridge has been attacked again, says Russian-installed governor

author: Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem
description:
Military incursion into Gaza, the first since ceasefire was agreed last October, comes as Eisenkot seeks to form government without Netanyahu

The Israeli military crossed into Hamas-controlled central Gaza on Wednesday in its first ground operation across the “yellow line” boundary since a fragile ceasefire was agreed last October, forcing dozens of displaced Palestinians to flee their tents.

Israeli tanks rolled along the Salah al-Din road, Gaza’s main north-south route, a day after the US-backed Board of Peace, a body overseeing the ceasefire, accused Israel and Hamas of failing to honour their commitments to end hostilities.

Continue reading...
title: Israeli tanks cross ‘yellow line’ boundary into Hamas-controlled central Gaza

author: Suzanne Wrack at the Cherry Red Records Stadium
description:
Chelsea were made to work hard for three Champions League points against a resilient Paris Saint-Germain side but their patience paid off, Veerle Buurman squeezing the ball in at the near post to put them, temporarily at least, at the top of the table in the league phase.

Buurman had stolen the show in Chelsea’s defeat of Manchester City at the weekend, coming on 12 minutes in and nullifying Khadija Shaw’s threat to be named player of the match and she was the hero under the lights with Chelsea doing everything but score prior to her goal.

Continue reading...
title: Veerle Buurman scrambles late WCL winner to push blunt Chelsea past PSG

author: Associated Press
description:
• 2027 season under threat amid dispute over salary cap

  • Commissioner says fans want a more equal game

MLB commissioner, Rob Manfred, has insisted owners will not budge from their demand for a salary cap, leaving the league on track for a lockout starting 2 December that could threaten the 2027 season.

“I can’t imagine the owners ratifying a deal that does not include a cap and floor,” Manfred said on Wednesday at a news conference during an owners meeting. Players say they will never accept a cap. The last time management proposed a cap in 1994, it led to a strike that lasted almost eight months and caused the cancellation of the World Series for the first time in 90 years.

Contin
title: MLB commissioner Manfred cites fan support for salary cap as baseball heads towards lockout

author: Nadeem Badshah
description:
Justice minister makes request to Google representatives in wake of 51-year-old’s prison message, according to Sky News

The government has reportedly asked Google to deactivate Russell Brand’s YouTube account after he was able to publish a message claiming his innocence following his conviction for sexual offences.

A justice minister met representatives from the technology company to make the request after social media firm Meta disabled the former comedian’s profiles on Instagram and Facebook, according to Sky News.

Continue reading...
title: UK government reportedly asks for Russell Brand’s YouTube account to be deactivated

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Disruption comes at critical moment, with Grand Theft Auto VI one of the most eagerly anticipated titles in history

PlayStation has suffered widespread network problems just hours before the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, one of the most eagerly anticipated titles in recent gaming history.

The disruption emerged Wednesday, causing frustrated players to flood social media with complaints about failed logins and server connection problems downloading games and updates.

Continue reading...
title: PlayStation suffers widespread network problems hours before release of GTA VI

author: Pablo Iglesias Maurer
description:
• US women’s head coach won Olympics in 2024

  • Hayes enjoyed trophy-laden tenure at Chelsea

The US women’s national team head coach, Emma Hayes, said she was “confident in the group that is being put together” to select her next counterpart for the men’s team – a group that includes her.

Speaking after announcing her team’s squad for the ­Concacaf championship and World Cup qualifier, Hayes shed light for the first time on her role in searching for Mauricio Pochettino’s replacement after the Argentinian decamped to Manchester United. US Soccer had previously said Hayes – alongside the federation CEO, JT Batson, the chief operating officer, Dan Helfrich, and Oguchi Onyewu, the vice-president of sporting – wo
title: Emma Hayes to assist in US Soccer hiring process for next USMNT coach

author: Editorial
description:
A trilateral gathering is good news for China and Russia, but bad for the US – and its traditional allies

“Historic” is a neutral descriptor, not a favourable one. Things can be unprecedented for good reason. Donald Trump’s meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China on Thursday will be the first time that the leaders of the US, China and Russia have gathered for talks as a trio. The trilateral on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is striking, but it is not an achievement.

The lack of a clear agenda is telling: the spectacle really is the substance. Mr Trump sees international affairs in terms of spheres of influence. This meeting reinforces the obvious conclusion for the rest of the world – that they don’t get to sit at the table, only to be on the plate. Mr Xi promotes the notion of a multipolar world. Others would be more
title: The Guardian view on the Trump, Xi and Putin meeting: it may be a first, but it’s not progress | Editorial

author: Ella Baron
description: Continue reading...
title: Ella Baron on the meeting between Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump – cartoon

author: Ben Quinn Political Correspondent
description:
Comments by Reform’s home affairs spokesperson raise questions about unity at the top of the party

Former Conservative defectors to Reform UK have been barred from shaping the party’s immigration policy, its home affairs spokesperson has claimed, excluding in effect the majority of the party’s MPs.

“If you are in the category of being concerned about [former Conservatives being involved in Reform], none of the above are going to be involved in immigration policy or borders policy,” Zia Yusuf told a podcast by the Spectator magazine.

Continue reading...
title: Ex-Tory defectors barred from shaping Reform UK’s immigration policy, says Yusuf

author: Rebecca Bailey in Shenzhen
description:
Chinese president greets US counterpart with rare hug before blockbuster trilateral meeting with Putin

China’s Xi Jinping rallied Asia-Pacific nations against trade protectionism on Wednesday morning before heading to the airport to welcome Donald Trump, whose administration has just further restricted advanced chip exports, with a rare hug.

The Chinese president spent Wednesday’s opening day of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit switching lanes between multilateralist and big-power politics, culminating in a group photo where he stood central among fellow leaders. He was flanked by Trump and Vladimir Putin – whose blockbuster trilateral meeting will dominate Thursday’s proceedings as the summit gets to its business end.

Continue reading...
title: Xi Jinping rallies against protectionism as he welcomes Trump to Apec summit

author: Guardian community team
description:
Grand Theft Auto VI has finally arrived. We’d like to hear your initial thoughts

It’s been 13 years in the making, and may be the most highly anticipated video game of all time. Grand Theft Auto VI has finally arrived.

The new instalment of the epic crime saga is said to have cost more than $1bn to make and is widely expected to break sales records: some predictions put total sales at 40m copies in its first three months.

Continue reading...
title: Tell us: are you playing Grand Theft Auto VI?

author: Anna Betts
description:
Democratic lawmakers ask if commerce secretary favored Nvidia to enrich his adult children and Cantor Fitzgerald

The US commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, faces mounting questions over his handling of the Nvidia affair as Democratic lawmakers demand answers over his family firm’s vast stake in the tech company.

Cantor Fitzgerald, the investment firm Lutnick ran for decades before joining the Trump administration, held shares in Nvidia worth “hundreds of millions of dollars” while Lutnick made key decisions affecting the tech firm’s ability to operate, according to Democrats on three key congressional committees.

Continue reading...
title: Democrats demand answers from Howard Lutnick about Nvidia and his family’s business

author: Dan Collyns in Ayacucho
description:
Renata Flores has earned global recognition for her music in Indigenous language whose speakers have at times faced social stigma

With her long black hair braided into beaded plaits, a delicate silver nose ring, and intricately patterned Andean textile draped around her chest above baggy, low-riding jeans, Renata Flores is a visual reflection of her music: a fusion of traditional and transgressive, old and new, rural and urban.

Nicknamed the “queen of Quechua rap”, Flores, 25, has earned global recognition for mixing Peru’s main Indigenous language and Andean instruments with the contemporary urban beats of trap, rap, hip-hop and reggaeton.

Continue reading...
title: The Quechua rapper and an artistic movement reclaiming language of the Incas

author: Adrian Chiles
description:
Not even a compelling TV drama can stop me from staring at my phone. But this urge started 40 years ago, with what was at first presented as a useful feature

I blame the shuffle button. That’s what started me on the long road to a thoroughly scattered mind – generally unable to focus on anything for more than a few minutes or even seconds. I was always a bit like this, hence an ADHD diagnosis in later life. But back in the day I still managed to read a lot of books, watch long films and listen to whole records at one sitting. Now? Not so much. Actually, hardly ever.

Even something on television that I’m really engaged in – a drama or a football match – can hold me for only a few minutes before I find myself scrolling on my phone looking for I know not what. I don’t know whether it’s because I’m drawn to the small phone screen, or rather that I find absorption with whatever I’m watching on the big flatscreen just too much to bear.
title: Instant gratification is ruining our lives – and for me it started with my CD player’s shuffle button | Adrian Chiles

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
Robert Garcia plans searches into Trump family finances, alleged DHS misconduct, and handling of Epstein files

The incoming Democratic chair of the powerful oversight committee in the House of Represenatives, has ordered a dozen relatives and allies of Donald Trump to preserve records before investigations he plans to open.

Robert Garcia sent 12 letters on Wednesday to prominent figures in the US president’s orbit, including his sons Donald Jr and Eric; son-in-law Jared Kushner; Vice-President JD Vance; and the attorney general, Todd Blanche.
title: Trump family and allies told to preserve records as Democrats prepare sweeping investigations

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Uncle of Iryna Zarutska, a 23-year-old who was murdered on the train, filed a wrongful death lawsuit against the city

Officials in Charlotte, North Carolina, have petitioned a judge to dismiss the wrongful death lawsuit over the murder of Iryna Zarutska, a 23-year-old Ukrainian refugee who was killed by a man on a light rail train in the city in August 2025.

Zarutska’s uncle, Frank Scott Haskell, who was hosting Zarutska and her family in Charlotte, filed the lawsuit against the city and its transit security company, Professional Security Services, claiming that Charlotte failed to take reasonable and available safety measures to prevent her murder.

Continue reading...
title: Officials seek dismissal of lawsuit over stabbing of Ukrainian refugee on train in Charlotte

author: George Francis Lee
description:
For more than a decade, GTA Online and its virtual California has hosted the criminal capers of millions of players. As many of them prepare to move on to GTA VI, they are marking the end of an era

  • Tell us: are you playing Grand Theft Auto VI?

The virtual streets of Grand Theft Auto Online’s Los Santos will be spared from their usual explosions and high-speed car chases tonight, as hundreds of players meet for a final journey across the video game’s world before the release of Grand Theft Auto VI at midnight.

Rockstar Games’ multiplayer criminal sandbox normally prompts hostility between its millions of players by giving them ample access to guns, bombs and fighter jets. But fans took it upon themselves to peacefully cruise acros
title: Players say goodbye to Grand Theft Auto V with one last drive

author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
description:
Attorney general says E1 settlement decision should not be taken by caretaker government led by Netanyahu

Israel has postponed issuing contracts for the construction of a large settlement on the West Bank seen as likely to render a two-state solution unviable, days after the UK imposed sanctions against building firms operating in the area.

Israeli diplomats insisted the move was not in response to the measures from Downing Street. Gali Baharav-Miara, the attorney general, said any decision on settlement expansion should not be taken by the caretaker government led by Benjamin Netanyahu but by whatever new administration was formed.

Continue reading...
title: Israel delays building contracts for West Bank settlement after UK sanctions

author: Micha Frazer-Carroll in the Bahamas
description:
During my visit to the Fuze Caribbean art fair in the Bahamas, I marvelled at how creators captured the complex nature of Caribbeanness

  • Don’t get The Long Wave delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

When I tell people I’m travelling to the Bahamas to report on Fuze Caribbean art fair, no one believes I’m really going for work. There are smirks and jokes about it being a tough life, about drinking from coconuts on the beach. The tourist gaze pervades global perceptions of the Caribbean. This week, I speak to the region’s artists about how they use images to speak back.

I have Antiguan and Jamaican heritage, so I’m familiar with the fantasies the Caribbean sparks, which Antiguan-American writer Jamaica Kinc
title: Am I Caribbean, or am I a tourist? How art helped me find the answer

author: Helena Horton
description:
Animal welfare charities criticise ‘backwards step’ on foie gras, production of which has been banned in UK since 2007

Ministers will drop plans to ban foie gras imports into the UK in order to smooth a trade deal with the EU that will be announced this week.

As first reported by the Financial Times, the proposed ban will be officially dropped on Friday when the government announces its sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) trade deal with the EU to reduce checks and paperwork on imports and exports of food and drink with the bloc.

Continue reading...
title: Ministers to drop foie gras imports ban to help seal EU food trade deal

author: David Conn and Felicity Lawrence
description:
Exclusive: Jury was never told that Prof Peter Hindmarsh was barred from practising over concerns for patients’ safety

A senior doctor whose evidence helped to convict Lucy Letby and who was held up by prosecutors as a pre-eminent expert was barred from treating patients during the trial over fears he posed a risk to their safety.

Prof Peter Hindmarsh, a specialist in hormones in children, was crucial to the crown’s argument that Letby had poisoned children by injecting insulin into fluid bags. But a Guardian investigation can reveal he was excluded from clinical practice in March 2023, five months before the end of the trial, by his employer, University College London hospitals trust (UCLH). Jurors were never told.

Continue reading...
title: Doctor whose evidence helped to convict Lucy Letby was barred from treating patients during trial

author: Hosted by Siobhán McSweeney , series producer Sophie King , research and social producer Avi Asher , Camera and edit Jamie Jackson , second camera Frankie Hill , guest booker Sam Taylor , executive producers Sarah Taylor Corby & James Tindale commissioning editor Elizabeth Cassin
description:
What does Lady Whistledown eat when nobody's watching? 


This week on Comfort Eating, Siobhán McSweeney is joined by the brilliant Nicola Coughlan, star of Derry Girls and Bridgerton, for a seriously fun catch-up involving comfort food, childhood nostalgia and some VERY questionable food combinations.


Nicola brings her ultimate comfort food to the table: think fusion - or perhaps it’s confusion.


There's also Diet Coke mixed with pickle juice (yes, really), stories about growing up in Galway, and her Supermac's Gold Card.


Plus, Nicola reflects on her journey into acting, drama school rejection, the early struggles of making it in London and how life changed after Derry Girls and Bridgerton.

Continue reading...
title: Nicola Coughlan on her favourite noodles, getting rejected from drama school and I Am Helen

author: Andrew Pulver
description:
The Crown star was reportedly an early favourite of director Denis Villeneuve, but ‘had reservations about the baggage associated with the role from the start’

Josh O’Connor, one of the actors on the final shortlist for the role of James Bond which was ultimately won by Robert Pattinson, was an early favourite of director Denis Villeneuve but pulled out of the contest before a decision was made, it has been reported.

Writing in Puck’s What I’m Hearing newsletter, Matthew Belloni (who correctly forecast that Pattinson would win the role) said that O’Connor “had reservations about the baggage associated with the role from the start” and pulled out shortly after his test.
title: Bond role was ‘Josh O’Connor’s to lose’ but actor pulled out of the running, report suggests

author: Presented by Madeleine Finlay , produced by Madeleine Finlay and Joshan Chana , graphics by Natalie Gegan
description:
Nasa sent the Voyager 1 and 2 probes into space almost 50 years ago to explore the outer reaches of our solar system. Now Voyager 1, the farthest human-made object from Earth, is about to reach a distance of one light-day away from our planet. To find out more about its astonishing journey, Madeleine Finlay hears from Jim Bell, a planetary scientist and professor at Arizona State University’s school of Earth and space exploration. He explains the seismic impact the mission has had on our understanding of the solar system, and where Voyager 1 could be heading now it has left the heliosphere

Continue reading...
title: Nasa’s Voyager 1 just reached a massive milestone in space - video

author: Peter Bradshaw
description:
Mason Reeves steals the show as an eight year old who stumbles across a sex assault but, despite strong performances, parts of the film feel contrived

Beth de Araújo’s new movie takes a very big swing, and it has won prizes and acclaim since its premiere at Sundance. I was unsure about some of the film’s high-concept ideas but the lead performance from its eight-year-old newcomer Mason Reeves is outstanding. Those concerned about spoilers had better look away.

Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan play Damien and Claire, a smart professional couple in San Francisco with a bright young daughter called Josephine, marvellously played by Reeves. Damien takes Josephine to Golden Gate Park one morning to play football (they turn out to enjoy watching the English Premier League on TV). She mischievously runs on ahead of her dad to a secluded spot in the park where Damien can’t immediately find her and it is there that Josephine witnesses a rape – not less horrifying for being filmed i
title: Josephine review – Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan ballast knotty drama about a child witness to a rape

author: Sarah Phillips
description:
The nights are drawing in, the temperature is dropping, festive overindulgence is on the horizon and it’s easy to get run down. Here’s some expert advice to help you safely through the season

Winter can be a challenging time, with bad weather, dark evenings, horrible bugs circulating, plus plenty of opportunities for overindulging. How can we avoid getting run down? Doctors share their tips for surviving the season, from saunas to screen blockers, light boxes to apples.

Continue reading...
title: Get vaccinated, don’t vape – and moisturise liberally! 10 doctors on how to avoid and treat winter ailments

author: Alia Waheed
description:
Tech companies urged to adapt moderation of photos online that can trigger violence against women in some countries

It was just a photo of a smiling girl in jeans and a vest top, the kind of outfit any young woman might wear in any country. But for Maniza*, a teenager from a conservative town in Pakistan who never leaves the house without her hijab, the selfie she took at home put her at very real risk of an “honour” killing.

“My family are really strict and I always wore a hijab. My father didn’t want me to stay in school but my mum pushed him. He said if I got into trouble, he would kill me. It wasn’t just words, he meant it,” she says.

Continue reading...
title: ‘My family would kill me if they saw it’: the ‘harmless’ images that can be deadly for women in Pakistan

author: Adrian Horton
description:
A staggering case of injustice is explored in the galling HBO documentary When a Witness Recants. The three subjects and producer Ta-Nehisi Coates explain how it unfolded

For most of his life, the writer Ta-Nehisi Coates would occasionally think of a chilling episode from his childhood in West Baltimore: almost exactly 43 years ago, on 18 November 1983, a 14-year-old boy named DeWitt Duckett was shot and killed in a hallway of Harlem Park junior high school in the middle of the afternoon, by an older teenager who stole his blue satin Georgetown jacket.

Coates was only eight years old at the time, too young to know the details, but old enough to perceive the collective horror around him. The sensational event – the first time a kid was killed inside a Baltimore public school, according to wall-to-wall local press – was a rupture in his child’s view of the world. “It was first time I had the sense that, oh, actually, I exist in a very dangerous world,” he told the Guardia
title: ‘We want our story to be told’: inside a shocking 36-year fight for justice in Baltimore

author: Guardian readers
description:
‘Deliciously dark’! ‘Not sexy enough’! Opinion is split on whether the star of Twilight and The Batman is the right choice to play 007. Here’s what some of you thought

So it’s official, Robert Pattinson will be James Bond. The long-awaited announcement of who would be stepping into 007’s tuxedo came as a surprise, and has divided opinion, judging by the more than 700 responses the Guardian received to a callout on the topic.

Readers were split on whether bosses at the franchise’s owner Amazon were right to give the role to the star of Twilight, Tenet and The Batman. Here are some of their views.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Worst decision in history’: Guardian readers shaken and stirred by the casting of Robert Pattinson as Bond

author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic Editor
description:
A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza

Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay, if the court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide against the Rohingya.

The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.

Continue reading...
title: Fears grow over US sanctions on ICJ judges ahead of Myanmar genocide ruling

author: Michael Donkor
description:
Translated into English in thrilling style, these interlinked stories of ambushes and vendettas vividly evoke the bitter conflict of the 1919-22 Greco-Turkish war

Nine interconnected tales about the violence of the 1919-22 Greco-Turkish war, and the struggles of its broken soldiers to reassimilate into civilian life, Gjak is something of a sensation. Originally written in Greek and Arvanitic, a dialect spoken by a Greco-Albanian ethnic group, and featuring characters from an unspecified Arvanite village, it was a hit in Greece in 2014 and comes to the UK in an agile translation by Siân Valvis. In her fascinating introductory note, Valvis writes of her attempt to capture the “unruly, galloping force” of Dimosthenis Papamarkos’s prose. She succeeds in thrilling style.

Delivered in a demotic, gossipy voice, these are rough-hewn stories of ambushes and vendettas, of brothers in arms being “closer than kin” and of lingering, sour regret. One of the translation
title: Gjak by Dimosthenis Papamarkos review – sensational tales of wartime Greek struggle

author: Jakub Krupa
description:
Boris Pistorius says comments from US official questioning the effectiveness of such attacks were ‘quite a stupid thing’

Germany’s defence minister, Boris Pistorius, has dismissed US criticism of Ukraine’s deep strikes into Russia as “quite a stupid thing”, speaking after the latest round of talks among Kyiv’s allies in Brussels.

US undersecretary of defence Elbridge Colby said yesterday that despite “the public conversation focusing on the spectacle of deep strikes,” they “have not been effective in driving an end to the war, nor do they contribute to blunting Russia’s advances on the frontline” (Europe Live, Tuesday).

“I want the Russian Federation to receive a clear signal: for every strike they launch against o
title: Germany hits out after US criticises Ukraine’s deep strikes into Russia – Europe live

author: Sean Ingle
description:
Surveys estimate 10 million minors globally use banned performance-enhancing drugs but suppliers are rarely brought to justice

Of all the many stories in Doping Top Secret: Children, a powerful new documentary from the German investigative team that helped expose massive Russian cheating in sport over a decade ago, one keeps replaying in my mind.

It involves an East German champion, who breaks his silence half a century on from his Olympic triumph to reveal how being pumped full of anabolic steroids at a young age accelerated his sexual development and, he believes, dramatically altered his behaviour and those of his teammates. “The system abused me as a young person for the good of the state,” says Hans-Georg Aschenbach, who won ski-jump gold in Innsbruck in 1976. Although nothing can prepare you for what he says about how the drugs affected his libido, and particularly what he would sometimes do before he jumped off a large ramp.
title: Child doping isn’t just cheating – it’s a global epidemic of abuse and exploitation | Sean Ingle

author: Laura Snapes
description:
Cher will take the legends slot at next year’s festival, which will also see debuts from Kraftwerk and Angine de Poitrine

• Read the lineup so far in full below

After fervent speculation about its headliners, the first batch of 2027 Glastonbury performers has been announced, and with it the youngest cohort of headliners this century.

This year’s edition brings two debut turns atop the Pyramid stage: North Shields singer-songwriter Sam Fender on Friday, and former boyband star turned global supernova Harry Styles on Saturday.

Continue reading...
title: Sam Fender, Harry Styles and Billie Eilish to be youngest Glastonbury headliners of 21st century

author: Rory Carroll Ireland correspondent
description:
Inquest-style inquiry concludes iron age remains are of 15- to 22-year-old female who may have been ritually sacrificed

A coroner’s investigation into Northern Ireland’s most venerable cold case has concluded that the victim was decapitated more than 2,000 years ago.

The inquest-style inquiry determined that Ballymacombs More Woman – the name given to iron age remains found in a County Derry bog three years ago – was between 15 and 22 years old when she was beheaded from behind with a bladed weapon.

Continue reading...
title: Body found in Derry bog decapitated more than 2,000 years ago, coroner finds

author: John Brewin
description:
Everton forward has magical talent and popularity to burn, but has come up against hard reality of the modern game

Thomas Tuchel has never called up the player he once claimed to love “everything about”. The reason for Jack Grealish’s omission from Tuchel’s first England squad in March 2025 was given as “he simply has no rhythm”.

Catch a falling star? Grealish was suspended by Everton for three matches following “a breach of club discipline”. Suggestions his loan from Manchester City might be cancelled were calmed by David Moyes. Last week, Grealish played in a behind-closed doors friendly against Derby before issuing an Instagram statement: “I want to apologise to the fans and everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.” Amid tabloid tales of karaoke nights and extended socialising, how close is the former boy wonder, now 31, to blowing it?
title: Jack Grealish recalls a golden age of mavericks – but football has moved on

author: Guardian sport
description:
Plus: clubs with roads on their team badges, most and fewest managers per league title, and more

  • Mail us with all of your questions and answers

“The Scotland men’s team’s highest Fifa ranking was 13th (in 2007) and the worst was 88th place (in 2005) – a difference of 75 positions,” writes Bogdan Kotarlic. “Is this the biggest gap between the best and worst ranking for one national team?”

The gap between Scotland’s best and worst Fifa rankings isn’t the biggest in men’s international football; in fact, Pete Tomlin calculates that a 75-place swing puts them joint 141st with Ghana and Seychelles. And, as Chris Lewis and others point out, there are a couple of other home nations who have had more dramatic swings. Wales and Northern Ireland both moved up 109 places: Wales from 117th to eighth under Gary Speed and then Chr
title: Swing when you’re winning? Biggest leaps across Fifa’s football rankings | The Knowledge

author: Oliver Hopkins
description:
The role of full-back has changed massively in recent years. We analyse how all 20 sides are approaching the position

By Opta Analyst

Overlapping. Underlapping. Inverted. Traditional. The role of full-back has evolved dramatically. Once a defensive-first position that provided some auxiliary attacking support, the role has developed into something far more multifaceted.

Just ask right-back Ben White, who – with Riccardo Calafiori on the left – has been an important figure in Arsenal’s superb start to the campaign. Talking a few years ago, he said: “Playing full-back the way [Mikel Arteta] wants is completely different to any other manager. To play full-back for him, you’ve got to be a centre-midfielder, a centre-back, a winger and a No 10.”

Continue reading...
title: Overlap, underlap or sit back? How Premier League teams use their full-backs

author: Mike Hytner
description:
• Zoric puts target on veteran teammate Gilmore’s back: ‘I want to be like her’

  • Peru win makes her first Indigenous Australian world champion in open category

With the surfing world her oyster, Leihani Zoric has set her sights stratospherically high after the 14-year-old stunned a star-studded field to be crowned the youngest ever ISA Open World Surfing Champion and claim a second world title this year.

Zoric, who was still 13 when she won the ISA under-18 world title in September, added a gold medal to her burgeoning individual palmarès with victory in Peru over the weekend, when she emerged triumphant ahead of established stars of the surfing world such as Stephanie Gilmore, Tyler Wright, Carissa Moore and Johanne Defay.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Ten is the minimum’: 14-year-old surfing champion Leihani Zoric aims for record world title haul

author: Associated Press
description:
The US secretary of state was speaking after Microsoft, major banks, and the National Security Agency were all affected by technical failures in recent days

US secretary of state Marco Rubio has sought to assure Americans that there’s “zero” information that the cascade of service outages – which have grounded flights, cut off work access, limited bank access and disrupted classified communications – are related to each other or to a malign actor.

In recent days, Microsoft, major US banks, American air traffic control systems and the National Security Agency
title: ‘Zero’ evidence that recent cascade of tech outages are linked, says Rubio

author: Chris Stein
description:
Republican incumbent beaten in race dominated by controversy over second candidate named Dan Sullivan

Democrat Mary Peltola will be Alaska’s next senator after beating the Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan, with the result called two weeks on from midterm elections which saw Donald Trump’s party lose ground across the country.

Peltola, a former US House lawmaker, is the first Democrat the state has elected to the Senate since 2008. Her victory comes just two years after Alaska voters unseated her while supporting Trump by a double-digit margin.

Continue reading...
title: Mary Peltola beats Republican Dan Sullivan in Alaska to give Democrats 56 Senate seats

author: Guardian Staff
description:
In Delhi, Hindy devotees congregated at the Yamuna River for the Chhath festival, wading through patches of toxic foam created by a mixture of pollutants including industrial chemicals and untreated sewage. The Chhath festival is observed by Indian and Nepalese Hindus honouring Lord Surya (the sun god) and the goddess Chhathi Maiya. The celebrations are meant to bring a prosperous life, fertility and protection.

Continue reading...
title: Delhi devotees brave river pollution as Chhath festival celebrated across India - in pictures

author: Raphael Rashid in Seoul
description:
South Korea has been gripped by revelations of AI-aided cheating, just days before more than half a million students are to sit high-stakes entrance exams

The integrity of South Korea’s career-defining university entrance exam has been thrown into doubt after the top scorer in a recent professional exam admitted using a concealed camera and AI to cheat.

On Thursday, more than half a million people, mostly school students, are due to sit the exam, known as the suneung, at 1,312 centres across the country. The exam runs for a gruelling eight hours over a single day and determines which university a candidate can attend and, in turn, their future prospects.
